- The internal vascular/pith tissue shows **extensive dark brown to near-black discoloration** running the full length
- The outer cortex remains green/normal
- The discoloration is centered in the vascular bundles and pith

**Reasoning:**
This classic presentation of cutting open a stem to reveal internal vascular browning/necrosis is the hallmark diagnostic feature of **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (*Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *michiganensis*). The very dark, extensive vascular discoloration throughout the entire interior of the stem is characteristic. Verticillium wilt would typically show lighter, more one-sided streaking; Bacterial Wilt (Ralstonia) would show slimy ooze. The deep black-brown coloration throughout the vascular tissue strongly aligns with bacterial canker.
